JUDGMENT 1.
At the request of learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent, the matter is heard on the application for condonation of delay as well as on merits.
2. This appeal arises from the judgment and award dated 06.01.2010 in LAC No.705/2007 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Belagavi ('the Reference Court', for short).
The claim petition is filed by the present appellant challenging the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer ('the SLAO', for brevity)
, is dismissed.
Thus, the claim for enhancement of compensation in Reference under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is rejected.
3. There is delay of 4680 days in filing the appeal.
I.A.1/2023 is filed to condone the delay invoking NC: 2023:KHC-D:10739 Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The respondents have not filed the objection to the said application.

However, the learned counsel for the respondents vehemently opposed the application for condonation of delay on the premise that the sufficient cause, as contemplated under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is not shown to condone the delay.

Thus, the respondents urged that the application has to be dismissed and consequently the appeal has to be dismissed.
4.
This Court has considered the application for condonation of delay.

There is no denial that the land bearing Survey No.72/1+2 measuring 2 acres 19 guntas and Survey No.72/7A measuring 1 acre 10 guntas of Anawal village, Badami Taluk, District Bagalkote, belonging to the present appellant were acquired for the public purpose by invoking the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
A preliminary notification in this regard was issued on 09.03.2004.
The SLAO passed award on 13.03.2007 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10739 awarding compensation of Rs.41,297/- per acre.
The claimant sought enhancement of compensation on the premise that the compensation awarded is wholly inadequate.

The Petition registered in LAC No.705/2007 and vide order dated 06.01.2010, the petition is dismissed, on the premise that the claimant has not led either oral or documentary evidence to support his claim.

Thereafter, the Reference Court concluded that no materials are Manappa S/O. Laxmappa Teggi vs The Slao, Grbc on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170082741/
2 available to show that the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) is inadequate.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petition is rejected.

5. The appellant in his affidavit accompanying the application seeking condonation of delay has averred that he was shocked by the inadequate compensation awarded on account of the compulsory acquisition and that he has no other lands, and he was not in a position to pay the court fee challenging the inadequate compensation awarded by the SLAO on account of the financial difficulty.
Hence he could NC: 2023:KHC-D:10739 not file the appeal before this Court is the ground urged to condone the delay.

6. Though the respondents have urged that sufficient grounds are not made out in the affidavit for condonation of delay, this Court has taken into consideration that the appellant has pleaded that he has no other lands other than the lands acquired.
7. It is also required to be noticed that the right to property is a constitutional right and the said right can be taken away only in the manner provided in law.
8. No documents are produced to show that the appellant has some other land and had the means to pay the court fee.
Moreover the reference Court has not applied its mind while confirming the award of the SLAO.
It has not assigned any reasons to confirm the award of SLAO except saying that the claimant has not led any evidence.
Reference Court has not analysed the award of the SLAO.

Though the State claims to have followed the procedure contemplated under law to acquire the property of the appellant, what is required to be borne in mind is the land loser should get just and fair compensation as contemplated under law.
10. There is no adjudication of the appellant's claim on merits, as the appellant did not lead evidence before the reference Court.

11. Considering the affidavit accompanying the application, the grounds urged in the appeal memo and the objection of the State, and keeping in mind that the appellant's right is a right guaranteed under Article 300A of the Constitution of India, this Court is of the view that an opportunity should be given to the appellant to hear the case on merits by condoning the delay.
Accordingly the delay is condoned.

12. For the reasons assigned to condone the delay and considering that the reference court has not NC: 2023:KHC-D:10739 considered whether the compensation awarded by the SLAO is a just and fair compensation, and has chosen to dismiss the petition technically on the ground that appellant has not lead any evidence, this Court is of the view that the impugned award is to be set aside,
permitting the appellant to lead the evidence in support of his claim before the Reference Court.

sentences.text:
However, it has to be noticed that there is a delay of 4680 days in filing the appeal and the beneficiary should not be burdened with interest for those 4680 days, in case the Reference Petition is allowed and compensation is enhanced.
14.
Thus, the appellant is not entitled to interest for 4680 days in case compensation is enhanced by the Reference Court.

15. With these observations, the delay of 4680 days in filing the appeal is condoned by allowing I.A.1/2023 and the impugned judgment and award dated NC: 2023:KHC-D:10739 06.01.2010 passed in LAC No.706/2007 on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) are set aside.
The matter is remanded to the Reference Court.
16. Appeal is allowed in part.
(i) The impugned judgment and award dated 06.01.2010 passed by the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Badami in LAC No.706/2007 are set aside and the matter is remanded to the Reference Court.
(ii) Since the matter is remanded to the Reference Court, Registry to return the admissible court fee to the appellant.

(iii) The Reference Court shall decide the claim petition on merits without being influenced by any of the observations made in this appeal, except the portion of the order denying the interest to the claimant.
(iv) All contentions are kept open.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10739 (v) Parties shall appear before the Reference Court on 09.10.2023 without awaiting any further notice from the Reference Court.
